decisions.question: Classify September customer deposits.
decisions.answer: Classify €90,000 September deposits as contract liabilities, not revenue.
evidence: E02 Contracts, Returns and Angry Customers
E09 CRM Export
decisions.aiProposal: defer the €60,000 NB-SEP and €30,000 FF-SEP receipts because the contracts record no delivery by 31 August.
decisions.independentChallenge: cross-checked both September deposits against the contract delivery dates and reached the same €90,000 liability conclusion.
decisions.studentReasoning: The contracts and CRM identify €60,000 and €30,000 as September deposits with no goods or services delivered by 31 August. Cash receipt therefore creates a €90,000 contract liability, not August revenue.

decisions.question: Classify New bank borrowing.
decisions.answer: Classify €50,000 new advance as loan liability.
evidence: E07 Loans, Owner Card and Legal Problems
E01 Bank Export August.csv and post-takeover bank confirmation
decisions.aiProposal: recognise the €50,000 bank advance as a loan because the signed agreement describes borrowing, not income.
decisions.independentChallenge: treated the bank agreement as higher-quality evidence than management’s label and independently concluded that the receipt is debt.
decisions.studentReasoning: The signed bank agreement calls the €50,000 receipt a loan advance. The bank description and the loan evidence outweigh management’s unsupported “strategic income” label, so the receipt is a liability.

decisions.question: Classify Packaging machine.
decisions.answer: Capitalize Pack-O-Matic at €60,000.
evidence: E03 Purchases Invoices and Goods Received
E06 Assets Repairs Leases
decisions.aiProposal: capitalise the €60,000 Pack-O-Matic because invoice A-910 identifies an installed machine available for use.
decisions.independentChallenge: confirmed that an installed packaging machine gives future benefit and agreed that the €60,000 is PPE.
decisions.studentReasoning: Invoice A-910 identifies a €60,000 packaging machine installed on 10 May. It is a controlled asset available for use, so cash is exchanged for PPE rather than creating an expense.

decisions.question: Classify Photo booth.
decisions.answer: Capitalize Regret Photo Booth at €20,000.
evidence: E03 Purchases Invoices and Goods Received
E06 Assets Repairs Leases
decisions.aiProposal: capitalise the €20,000 Regret Photo Booth because invoice P-404 identifies equipment available for use.
decisions.independentChallenge: confirmed that the photo booth was available for use and agreed that the €20,000 is PPE.
decisions.studentReasoning: Invoice P-404 identifies the €20,000 photo booth and confirms it was available for use on 10 May. It is a long-lived operating asset, so the payment is capitalised as PPE.

decisions.question: Classify Machine belt and calibration.
decisions.answer: Expense €10,000 belt and calibration work as repairs.
evidence: E03 Purchases Invoices and Goods Received
E06 Assets Repairs Leases
decisions.aiProposal: expense €10,000 because invoice R-771 says the work restored normal output and did not extend useful life.
decisions.independentChallenge: focused on the invoice language “restored normal output” and agreed that the €10,000 is repair expense.
decisions.studentReasoning: Invoice R-771 says the €10,000 belt, cleaning and calibration restored normal output without increasing capacity or useful life. That evidence supports repair expense rather than capital expenditure.

decisions.question: Classify Owner villa deposit.
decisions.answer: Classify €70,000 villa payment as owner distribution.
evidence: E07 Loans, Owner Card and Legal Problems
E01 Bank Export August.csv and post-takeover bank confirmation
decisions.aiProposal: classify the €70,000 villa reservation as a distribution because the villa is personally owned and no business meeting occurred.
decisions.independentChallenge: verified the founder’s personal ownership and absence of a business meeting; it agreed this is not marketing or payroll.
decisions.studentReasoning: The bank entry is for a €70,000 villa reservation in the founder’s personal name, and the case records no customer meeting. It is a distribution: cash and total assets fall €70,000 and equity falls €70,000, with no profit effect.

decisions.question: Classify Owner card spending.
decisions.answer: Classify €40,000 owner-card spending as owner distribution.
evidence: E07 Loans, Owner Card and Legal Problems
E01 Bank Export August.csv and post-takeover bank confirmation
decisions.aiProposal: classify €40,000 owner-card spending as a distribution because no business purpose is evidenced.
decisions.independentChallenge: found no business evidence for the owner-card spending and agreed it is an equity distribution.
decisions.studentReasoning: The loan and owner-card evidence identifies €40,000 of other owner card spending with no business purpose. It is a distribution: cash and total assets fall €40,000 and equity falls €40,000, with no profit effect.

decisions.studentReasoning: Warehouse records specify €405,000 of physical product materials consumed on valid delivered sales. Those materials are no longer an asset and are recognised in COGS; the separate €9,000 count variance remains disclosed.

decisions.studentReasoning: The payroll evidence identifies €80,000 for event delivery. Because it directly fulfils completed events, it is service COGS rather than selling or administration expense.

decisions.studentReasoning: The asset schedule supports €24,000 depreciation for the period on PPE available for use. Depreciation consumes the asset’s carrying amount without a current-period cash outflow.

decisions.question: Classify Bad receivable.
decisions.answer: Recognize €18,000 bad-debt expense/allowance.
evidence: E02 Contracts, Returns and Angry Customers

decisions.aiProposal: record an €18,000 specific allowance because R-17 was in liquidation with no recovery expected.
decisions.independentChallenge: treated the post-year-end liquidation notice as adjusting evidence of the 31 August condition and agreed the €18,000 allowance.
decisions.studentReasoning: The R-17 liquidation notice says no distribution is expected and confirms a condition existing at 31 August. The €18,000 receivable is therefore specifically impaired, reducing profit, receivables and equity by €18,000.

decisions.question: Classify Damaged stock.
decisions.answer: Recognize €22,000 inventory write-down.

decisions.aiProposal: write down €22,000 water-damaged inventory to nil because the warehouse count says it is unsaleable.
decisions.independentChallenge: accepted the warehouse’s nil saleable value and agreed that the disposal quote does not establish a provision.
decisions.studentReasoning: Warehouse evidence says the water-damaged stock has no saleable value and gives its carrying value as €22,000. The €2,000 disposal quote is not a present obligation, so only the €22,000 inventory write-down is recorded.

decisions.question: Classify Probable legal claim.

decisions.independentChallenge: accepted the external lawyer’s 31 August probability assessment and agreed the €25,000 best estimate.
decisions.studentReasoning: External counsel confirmed at 31 August that the employee claim was probable and its best estimate was €25,000, within a €20,000–€30,000 range. This supports a €25,000 expense and provision.

decisions.question: Use claimed management profit for earn-out
decisions.answer: Do not use management’s €312,000 profit for earn-out; use corrected provisional accounts.
evidence: E01 Bank Export August.csv and post-takeover bank confirmation
E11 Management P&L workbook
E10 Email and WhatsApp Dump
decisions.aiProposal: reject management’s €312,000 earn-out figure and use the corrected €65,000 provisional profit.
decisions.independentChallenge: agreed that management’s €312,000 claim lacks evidence support and that valuation must use the €65,000 corrected amount.
decisions.studentReasoning: Management’s €312,000 earn-out profit is not supported by the bank, contract, warehouse, payroll and legal evidence. The corrected €65,000 provisional profit is €247,000 lower and is the only supportable valuation basis.

reconciliations.name: Supplier balances
reconciliations.status: €45,000 opening payable plus €459,000 purchases less €378,000 cash paid equals €126,000 closing payables.

uncertainties: €9,000 difference between inventory cost roll-forward and saleable physical-count values.
Opening supplier payable of €45,000 is inferred from the supplier roll-forward and requires remittance confirmation.
No insurance policy, payment, prepayment, or consumption evidence was supplied.
Legal claim range is €20,000–€30,000; €25,000 is the best estimate.
€2,000 disposal quote is disclosed but not recorded as a present obligation.

boardRecommendation.summary: Use the corrected provisional accounts, not management’s €312,000 claimed profit, for valuation decisions.
actions: Move September deposits to contract liabilities.
Reconcile supplier remittances and inventory variance.
Tighten credit controls and pursue the R-17 balance.
